myths: S01: Fresha 'six of 22 services shown above the fold' called out as the strongest corroboration point in the synthesis does not reproduce: an independent re-fetch of the same live URL returned 4 shown before 'See all', not 6. The claim is downgraded to a range and the 'strongest evidence point' superlative is removed; the band-4-7 fit still holds (at the floor) but is not the clean convergence the draft claimed.

S01: The 50ms first-impression citation is likely swapped: the well-established primary source for '50ms to form a first impression of a webpage' is Lindgaard, Fernandes, Dudek, Brown (2006), not Tuch et al. (2012) IJHCS. The draft's own note says it 'corrected' an earlier hci-basel.ch/2007 citation to Tuch 2012, but Tuch's own lab is hosted at hci-basel.ch and the paper's actual exposure duration could not be confirmed (access blocked). Repointed the 50ms claim to Lindgaard 2006; kept Tuch 2012 as a narrower, duration-unspecified claim.

S01: Treatwell '~60% text / 40% visual' self-estimate does not reproduce: an independent re-fetch of the same page estimated 80-85% text / 15-20% visual. Both are ungrounded LLM eyeball estimates, not pixel measurements. Softened to a qualitative claim, tier CONV to T3.

S01: Booksy's documented profile structure does not explicitly itemize 'staff photos' as a discrete block (only 'portfolio / showcase your best work'); softened from an exact 7-item match to an approximate one.

S01: Uber 'internal design critique flagged as info present but not prioritized' is an unverifiable narrative claim sourced only to a tertiary teardown site, not a primary Uber document; downgraded CONV to T3 and flagged as weak, not cut, since it does not carry independent weight in the prior anyway.

S02: Uber bento claim overstated its sourcing: BGR/9to5Mac/CNET/Uber-Newsroom coverage of the 2023 redesign confirms only 'simplified homescreen, two prominent options: rides and Eats delivery, fewer taps' -- it does NOT use the words 'grid' or 'bento', and does not describe the destination-history section as staying a plain list. The visual bento-grid framing is a screenshot/scout interpretation layered onto press text that only describes simplification. Downgraded from a press-sourced T3 claim to a CONV-tier scout observation and the attribution language corrected so it is not misread as the outlets themselves calling it bento.

S02: The two stats already flagged MYTH by the draft ('67% of top-100 ProductHunt SaaS use bento', '15-25% higher mid-page engagement from bento') are correctly unsourced/untraceable and correctly excluded from proposed_addition's actual prose -- confirmed as properly quarantined, not smuggled into the shipped text. No action needed beyond confirming the quarantine held.

S03: "A DEV Community six-month retrospective names calm-design/anti-maximalism as the trend that stuck" is fabricated. The article (dev.to/studiomeyer_io, "Web Design Trends 2026: What Actually Held Up After Six Months") is real but says the opposite: bento grids and dark mode are what held up (denser/graphic patterns, not restraint); kinetic typography, glassmorphism 2.0, and organic blobs are what underdelivered. It never mentions calm design. This was cited as directional support for Solen's restraint lock when the source does not say that.

S03: "Showit and Figma Resource Library document a 96-128px section-gap shift" is an invented number. The Showit article (showit.com/business-growth/2026-web-design-trends-you-need-to-know) exists and was read directly; its only spacing guidance is a relative '20% more whitespace around the headline' tip, no pixel figures anywhere.

S03: "1140-1280px max content width per the Showit roundup" mis-cites its source; Showit does not mention a max-width figure at all. The number itself is a real, independently-known industry convention (Bootstrap 1140/1200px containers etc.), just not from the article it was attributed to.

S03: "involve.me explicitly frames fewer/larger sections with bigger gaps as a named 2026 trend" overstates its source; the article (involve.me/blog/landing-page-trends), read directly, treats whitespace only as a generic best practice (citing Google's homepage), with no explicit fewer-sections framing and no pixel numbers.

S03: Fresha/Booksy/Treatwell hero-height cited as CONV-tier (25-30%, 'live teardown') overstates both the method and the number. Live re-fetch this pass reads Fresha's hero at roughly 40-50% and Treatwell's at 30-40%, both above the claimed band; Booksy's fraction wasn't determinable. Neither the original synthesis nor this verify used actual pixel measurement (Playwright/getComputedStyle, this project's own site-teardown standard) -- both relied on AI-summarized page reads, which does not support a CONV/high-confidence tier.

S03: Doctolib's '5-10% of page height' hero figure is unconfirmed; WebFetch on doctolib.fr returned only footer/nav markup, the actual hero was never seen by either the original synthesis or this verify pass.

S04: Refuted: "Every search/filter zero-result CTA scouted is a solid brand-color fill; no neutral-outline precedent found" (in real_world_evidence, the BOUNDARY paragraph, and the taste_lab_probe framing). Re-scouted via Mobbin: Skyscanner's "Clear all filters" on its zero-flights screen is a neutral-outline pill (white bg, hairline border, blue text), not a fill. GitHub's "Reset search filters" is a plain blue text link with no button at all. Walmart's "We couldn't find a match" screen ships with NO CTA whatsoever. Only Too Good To Go (teal fill) and OpenSea ("Back to all items", blue fill) actually confirm the brand-fill pattern. The field is mixed, not a wall Solen alone would be breaking.

S04: Overstated: CRED's empty-trips illustration is described as "single-ink-outline" / monochrome. Re-checked via Mobbin: it is a black-line illustration WITH color fill (tan/beige compass shape, red/pink accent sparkles), not strictly monochrome ink-line. The lowercase headline and solid-black CTA parts of the claim hold; the illustration-style part does not.

S04: Stale number: EmptyStateDiscovery banner cited as "200px" (from the component doc's prose, both in the real_world_evidence entry and the "~25% of an 812px viewport" computed number). The live component code (app/[locale]/_components/profile/EmptyStateDiscovery.tsx line 73) actually renders h-[220px], not 200px. Recomputed: 220/812 = ~27%, not 25%. Still lands inside the claimed 15-40% band so the conclusion survives, but the cited number was wrong and traced to a stale doc rather than the live code.

S05: Container-query browser-support stat (~94% as of December 2025) is chronologically inconsistent with ground truth: caniuse.com's own live global usage-weighted figure (checked this pass) is 92.6% as of its current June-2026 snapshot. Browser support only grows over time, so a December-2025 figure should be LOWER than 92.6%, not higher at ~94%. The named secondary sources (LogRocket, DEV Community, UXPin) could not be independently re-verified this pass (WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-verification), so the specific magnitude is unconfirmed and directionally suspect. Softened in verified_addition to 'over 90%' with the caniuse contradiction noted rather than repeating the precise 94% figure.

S05: The 'TENSION FLAGGED' section drops a qualifier that is present in the actual locked line. LOCKFILE:856 reads `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3 lg:grid-cols-4 (2-col when map open)`, not a bare unconditional ladder. Both live Fresha and Airbnb renders this pass showed their grids WITH the map panel open, holding 2 columns, which is exactly what the Solen literal already specifies for the map-open case. The draft characterizes this as a flat, unexplained mismatch against the Fresha/Airbnb reference; it is at minimum an incomplete characterization, since the map-open branch may already match. The genuinely untested question is what the ladder does in the map-CLOSED state, which neither this stream's scouting nor this verification pass checked. Corrected in verified_addition and moved the open question to residual_risks with the accurate framing.

S05: The retroactive-grounding claim for Solen's `DateTimePicker` overstates its own component doc. Reading `_design-system/components/DateTimePicker.md` directly: `dateLayout="calendar"` vs `"strip"` is a PER-PRODUCT-CONTEXT selection (search page always uses calendar, booking flow always uses strip), not a viewport-breakpoint-driven collapse of one field into a summary pill the way PRIOR 4 describes for Fresha/Airbnb/Booking.com. The component is real and the 'don't build a second date picker' lock is real, but citing it as evidence for the RESPONSIVE reflow prior conflates two different kinds of mode selection. Softened in verified_addition to describe it as a precedent for per-product (not per-breakpoint) compound-control mode selection, which is what it actually demonstrates.

S05: The T3 'general web consensus on Airbnb's 6-5-4-3-2-1 column collapse' entry in real_world_evidence is directly contradicted by this stream's own T2 live-render finding (2-col hold through 768, drop straight to 1 at 375, no smooth multi-step descent), which I independently reconfirmed this pass. It is correctly kept out of the prose/proposed_addition and correctly tiered below the T2 direct observation, but sitting in the same evidence table as if it were corroborating rather than contradicted is misleading on a skim. Flagged in residual_risks for removal or an explicit 'contradicted by direct observation' note rather than deletion from verified_addition (owner call, not mine to silently cut).

S06: "highest-traffic imagery-bearing surface" applied to the search-results grid implies real usage/traffic data that does not exist: Solen is pre-launch with no real customers (memory: project_prelaunch_no_real_customers.md), so no analytics back a traffic ranking among surfaces. Softened in verified_addition to a funnel-position argument (first major imagery-bearing surface after home, not yet covered by PHOTO_STRATEGY.md) instead of an implied traffic metric. Not a myth_screen table hit (that table is scoped to conversion/retention percentages), but the same reality-over-memory / no-fabricated-data discipline applies.

S07: Foundey 'Stepper UI Best Practices' tiered T2 in the draft is actually a startup design agency's uncredentialed marketing blog with no cited study behind its 300ms claim, published the day before this session; downgraded to CONV.
S07: The ~70.22% cart-abandonment stat (digidrub.com) was already correctly caught as MYTH and correctly kept out of the proposed addition by the original synthesis; verified this catch is sound.

S07: LOCKFILE line-range citation for the 40ms stagger rule (1413-1420) points at the wrong section (sheet physics/shared-element rules); the real rule is at section 16.4, line approximately 1434. Locator error, not a fabricated rule, corrected in verified_addition.

S08: Uber Base 'CI linting blocks a new token merge until it passes WCAG and brand-guideline checks': unverifiable. Checked Uber's own Base Web launch blog post (uber.com/blog/introducing-base-web) and the uber/baseweb GitHub README directly — neither mentions any such CI/lint gate. This was the load-bearing fact behind the whole 'ENFORCEMENT PARALLEL' paragraph, so it cannot ride as a confirmed CONV citation; downgraded to T3/unverified and the enforcement paragraph rewritten to stand on Solen's own drift-check gate alone, not on an unconfirmed claim about Uber's pipeline.

S08: W3C DTCG 2025.10 spec described as 'stable Oct 2025': false framing. Live-fetched the actual spec page (designtokens.org/TR/drafts/format/) — it is explicitly labeled 'a preview draft... do not implement anything in this document,' a Draft Community Group Report (not W3C Standards Track), dated June 17 2026 in its current form. 'Stable' is the wrong word for a document that carries a do-not-implement warning; corrected to 'an evolving Draft Community Group Report, not a finished standard.'

S08: Atlassian's 'Foundation.Property.Variant.State' naming grammar: could not confirm this four-word label is Atlassian's own documented terminology (atlassian.design's token pages returned empty JS shells on fetch, no server-rendered content available). The underlying token examples cited (color.background.danger.bold, color.icon.success) match real, recognizable Atlassian token shapes from general knowledge, but the formal grammar name itself looks like the synthesis's own paraphrase rather than a quotable Atlassian term. Softened attribution so the naming discipline is not presented as an official Atlassian-coined phrase.

S08: myth_screen table check: zero hits. This stream cites no psychology/conversion statistics (2000% samples, 70-90% defaults, loss-aversion 2x, jam study, $300M button, retention multipliers, Amazon 100ms, Duolingo DAU, UGC 4x) — it is a design-tokens generative-gap stream, so the psychology myth table does not apply to any number in it. Confirmed clean on that axis.

S09: The draft's central T1 claim ('Fresha search card structure and density bands', sourced to 'fresha.com/search, live-rendered this session') is factually inverted. Live re-check this pass of the SAME session's already-open Fresha tabs (tab-3 and tab-8, both at the real /search results view with '9 venues within map area' + Filters + persistent map, screenshotted at 800x450) shows each search-result card actually carries: photo carousel + name + distance/address + category + (rating when present) + THREE inline priced/duration services (e.g. 'Haarschnitt, 30 min, CHF 40') + a 'View N matching services' link. That is a price-led, service-preview card, structurally closer to what the draft itself labels 'the Booksy pattern Solen should reject' than to the thin no-price card the draft describes. The thin card (photo + name + rating + address + category + review count, no price) is real, but it is Fresha's HOMEPAGE recommendation carousel (fresha.com root, confirmed via tab-1), not its search-results page.

S09: Because of the inversion above, the draft's 'Booksy ~8-10 fields/card vs Fresha ~5 fields/card (rejected-density contrast)' number is backwards: the actual Fresha search card is at least as field-dense as Booksy's (name + distance + category + up to 3 priced/timed services + a service-count link), not the sparse 5-field baseline claimed.

S09: Pinterest '~3.3 rows (6-7 tiles) visible per 812px fold' is presented as if pixel-measured. Mobbin screen captures (re-pulled this pass) support 'roughly 3 rows' qualitatively but not a decimal-precision figure; the '.3' reads as false precision dressed as a measurement, not an actual measurement.

S10: The '5 students' validation figure for Lok/Feiner/Ngai (IUI 2004) is not merely unverified, it is absent. I pulled the actual open-access PDF (columbia.edu/~lok/papers/balance.pdf, confirmed via DBLP conf/iui/LokFN04): the paper reports ZERO human subjects. Its 'Results' section (6) is a computational test-harness demo (BalanceManager screenshots, timing benchmarks) with no user study of any kind, let alone a 5-student one. This number should be cut outright, not hedged.

S10: The draft claims the proposed centroid-vs-geometric-center formula 'matches' Lok/Feiner/Ngai's model. Reading the actual paper: it does NOT compute a centroid offset from center at all. It builds a per-pixel WeightMap, downsamples via an image pyramid, and evaluates CRYSTALLOGRAPHIC balance (uniformity of weight across the whole map, compared against a uniform reference), using row/column sum derivatives to suggest move-directions, not a single weighted centroid minus frame-center number. The paper is real and on-topic (visual weight assigned per element, used to grade a layout) but 'formula shape matches' overstates the fidelity; it is a loose inspiration, not a derivation.

S10: The Jahanian paper is misattributed to 'MIT CSAIL.' DBLP confirms it is Ali Jahanian, S.V.N. Vishwanathan, Jan P. Allebach, 'Learning visual balance from large-scale datasets of aesthetically highly rated images,' SPIE Human Vision and Electronic Imaging 2015 (doi 10.1117/12.2084548), a Purdue-era paper (Allebach is Purdue faculty; HVEI is an SPIE venue). Jahanian's later MIT CSAIL affiliation postdates this specific paper by years; citing it under an MIT CSAIL byline is a false institutional tag.

S11: American Airlines checkout screen (mobbin.com/screens/886d6a4b-8cb6-4b50-9a5b-8fa3473c4374) cannot be located in Mobbin's catalog. Three separately-worded targeted mcp__mobbin__search_screens queries ("checkout passenger form with trip total price", "website screen", "flight booking") all returned zero American Airlines results, surfacing Booking.com / Kiwi.com / Tripadvisor / KAYAK / Navan / TravelPerk / Expedia / Klook instead. This was the draft's single most load-bearing counter-example (the only cited external violation of the ink-price lock, with an invented-looking $87.40 figure). It does not survive a direct catalog check and reads as a hallucinated screen ID. Cut entirely.

S11: HotelTonight sign-up screen (mobbin.com/screens/e2271701) also cannot be located. A targeted search for "HotelTonight sign up form dark theme" returned Fey, Cursor, Better Stack, Open, Basedash, no HotelTonight anywhere. Second app in the eight-screen set that fails a direct catalog check; the "dark theme, purple non-blue accent" claim is unverifiable and reads as fabricated. Cut entirely.

S11: The Airbnb Rausch 'one or two moments' quote attributed to github.com/kwakseongjae/oh-my-design does not appear in that source. Direct fetch of design-md/airbnb/DESIGN.md in that repo shows the actual text is 'Rausch is a current identity accent, not an inferred fill for every CTA' and 'Do not turn Rausch into a default fill for every control', a real but more general restraint claim with no 'one or two' quantification anywhere. The specific number was invented and presented as if quoted. The repo itself is also an AI-generated brand-reference library bundled with a coding-agent CLI tool, not a human design-team teardown, so even the general claim is a lower-confidence secondary source than the Uber superdesign.dev piece, which checked out clean.

S11: Peerspace's actual booking-flow commit CTA ('Request to Book') is a solid purple/violet fill, not solid black as the draft claims. Confirmed via direct Mobbin screenshots of the real Peerspace checkout flow: the black-filled segmented toggle claim is correct, but the CTA-color claim is wrong. The 'zero blue' claim itself still holds, purple is not blue, but the specific CTA-color detail needs correcting.

S12: Galen Framework 'default ~12px max mismatch / 30px scan region' for alignment tolerance: REFUTED. Fetched galenframework.com/docs/reference-galen-spec-language-guide directly. It does confirm real alignment assertions ('aligned horizontally all/top/centered') with a configurable per-check error-rate tolerance for near-miss pixels (example given: 'one object is by 1px higher than the other'), but it does NOT publish a fixed default of 12px for that tolerance. The separate 'analyze-offset N' parameter the draft cited as the tolerance mechanism is actually for IMAGE-DIFF offset search (finding the best-fit pixel shift between two screenshots), and its '30' default is a COLOR-difference tolerance for that image comparison, not a spatial alignment mismatch in px. The draft conflated two unrelated Galen features and invented specific numbers (12px, 30px) that are not in the source. Cut from verified_addition; the mechanic (edge-equality + configurable tolerance) stays cited as CONV, the fabricated defaults do not.

S13: Uber 'Base Counter' tool / daily-CD auto-ticketing / 'Feature Review Readiness' step: cited at CONV tier (implying a confirmed real observation) but could not be found via Bing search, direct URL guesses at uber.com/blog, or the current Uber blog listing (checked April-June 2026 posts, no match). The level of invented-sounding specificity (a named internal tool, a named review-step title) is a classic hallucination signature. Downgraded to unconfirmed; cut from the load-bearing 'two-stage pattern' evidence and kept only as an unverified aside.

S13: Chromatic/Percy 'the PR literally cannot merge while unresolved': Chromatic's own docs (fetched) state PR checks show status but a team must explicitly configure them as REQUIRED branch-protection checks in GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket for merge to actually block. The mechanism is real and common practice, but the draft stated it as automatic/inherent. Softened to note the required-check configuration step.

S13: Eleken '17-step' pre-handoff checklist: the exact page (eleken.co/blog-posts/design-qa-checklist) 404'd and no search budget remained to relocate it. The specific count '17' is unconfirmed and dropped from the sourced claim; kept only as 'a published numbered pre-handoff checklist exists in this genre' at CONV, not the precise step count.

S13: Figma 'AI design review assistant' shipped at Config 2026: already correctly tagged T3 in the draft, but zero corroboration turned up on two Bing searches and a direct figma.com/config/ fetch (404). Kept at T3 but the 'Config 2026' launch specificity is flagged explicitly as unconfirmed rather than presented as an establishable 2026 product fact.

S13: Draft's OPEN CAVEAT list ('only browser-verify-gate.sh, pre-build-exists-check.sh, pre-commit-graveyard.sh, pre-component-edit-pixel-spec.sh, pre-edit-drift-gate.sh, pre-edit-removed-check.sh, user-prompt-binary-triggers.sh are wired') is factually wrong: settings.json actually wires roughly 24 unique hook commands across SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop, including two OTHER Stop hooks already blocking turn-end (visual-deliverable-gate.py, recurrence-harden-gate.py) that the draft's list omits entirely. The core finding (mockup-floors-gate.py itself does not exist anywhere in the worktree, confirmed by direct grep/find) still holds and is the important part; the enumerated 'only these are wired' list does not and is corrected.

S14: Stitch Fix Style Shuffle volume: draft cites '1B+ ratings' but Stitch Fix's own newsroom post and LinkedIn material state '10 billion interactions' / 'over 10 billion item ratings' -- the draft's number is off by 10x. Corrected to 10 billion+ in verified_addition, still tagged CONV (self-reported, not audited).

S14: Stitch Fix '80%+ of 4M+ customers' figure: two search engines (DuckDuckGo, Bing) returned no Stitch Fix source stating any percentage of any customer count uses Style Shuffle. This specific figure could not be traced to any publication and is cut from verified_addition rather than softened -- it reads like an invented precision number attached to a real program.

S14: ScienceDirect 'LLM-assisted hybrid interfaces for remote repertory grid interviews' / 'Q-Survey' citation: could not be located via two independent search engines under any phrasing. This is very likely a hallucinated or misremembered citation, not a T3 finding. Downgraded to MYTH (unconfirmed citation) and removed from the source list and the 'active research direction' claim in verified_addition; the Kelly/Fransella methodology stands on its own without it.

S14: The FORMULA's '2 consecutive triads yield zero new poles' stopping rule and 'typically 6-10 triads for an 8-10 element pool' figure are presented as T2-sourced (attributed directly to Fransella/Bell/Bannister). The manual's real, confirmable claim is only the general concept 'run to saturation, not a fixed count' -- it is not confirmable that the manual specifies '2 consecutive' or '6-10' as exact numbers. Re-tagged CONV (a reasonable operational default inspired by the T2 concept) rather than T2 itself.

S14: The staircase's '3 reversals, mean of last 3' stop rule is presented as a direct T1/T2 Cornsweet convention. Cornsweet 1962 (confirmed real, American Journal of Psychology vol 75) describes continuing 'until many reversals are obtained around the value to be estimated' -- it does not specify 3 as the count; classic staircase practice often runs 6-8 reversals for precision. The specific cutoff of 3 is re-tagged CONV (a simplification for a fast, low-stakes subjective probe), with the general reversal-averaging mechanism staying T1.

S15: NN/g "Dangerous UX: Consequential Options Close to Benign Options" is cited in sources[] as a named canonical NN/g article/doctrine (T2). I could not find this article on nngroup.com's own article index, and targeted web/search checks (Bing, DuckDuckGo, Google) returned no corroboration of this exact title as an NN/g-authored piece. This is the same failure pattern the myth_screen guards against: a specific claim dressed in a prestigious org's name without a traceable citation. Downgraded to CONV (a real, well-observed practitioner convention, independently supported by the 8-app Mobbin convergence in this same draft) rather than verified NN/g doctrine. Do not cite this as "NN/g names X as a top-10 mistake" in the shipped RATIONALE entry without a working URL.

S15: Apple HIG's "60x60pt on visionOS" figure could not be verified this session: Apple's HIG pages are JS-rendered and returned only page titles to WebFetch, and no secondary source corroborated the specific visionOS number (the general 44x44pt iOS/iPadOS figure is well-corroborated and kept at T1, but the visionOS addendum is unverified, not confirmed-false, and should not be treated as settled until directly checked).

S16: The '40.4% average token coverage across 375 audited production sites' figure does not appear anywhere in the zeroheight Design Systems Report 2026 (that report is a 147-practitioner stability survey: 8% 'very stable' + 34% 'unstable' + 10% 'very unstable' = 44%, no site-audit coverage metric at all). The 375-sites/coverage numbers were pulled from a DIFFERENT study and glued onto the zeroheight citation, a genuine stat-conflation across two unrelated sources.

S16: The '375 sites, only 7.5% got it right' design-token-drift study is misattributed to 'Design Systems Collective' (designsystemscollective.com does not resolve, DNS failure on direct fetch). The real publisher is OverlayQA (overlayqa.com/blog/design-token-drift-study/), and the real headline stat is '90%+ token coverage puts a site in the top 7.5%', not a generic 'got it right' framing.

S16: OverlayQA's drift taxonomy actually names FIVE subtypes (token, component-variant, pattern, documentation, behavioral drift), not three; the draft cited three real ones without flagging that two more exist, an incomplete-taxonomy presentation.

S16: The Nielsen '249 usability problems, refined 1994' fact is real and quoted correctly, but does not appear on the cited URL (nngroup.com/articles/consistency-and-standards); it lives on nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/. Citation pointer error, not a false fact.

S17: NN/g 'Proximity' article claimed to 'offer an illustrative monotonic ladder: 4px within compound controls, 8px within groups, 16px between groups, 32px between sections, 64px major divisions' -- FALSE on direct fetch of nngroup.com/articles/gestalt-proximity/. The article is purely qualitative (Gestalt proximity, whitespace unites/separates); it contains zero pixel values or tiered numeric guidance. The ladder was invented and dressed up as an NN/g claim (CONV tier, social/trend scout). This is a fabricated-attribution pattern, not a weak-source pattern -- downgrade to MYTH/fabricated-attribution and strike the specific numbers from anything citing NN/g as the source.

S17: 1.25 spacing-ratio floor claimed to be 'borrowed by analogy from... two spacing-scale-construction essays (EightShapes, Utopia.fyi)' that supposedly recommend geometric steps for distinctness -- overstated on direct fetch. EightShapes' 'Space in Design Systems' (medium.com/eightshapes-llc/space-in-design-systems-188bcbae0d62) explicitly worked example uses a ~2x doubling progression (16/8/4/2 down, 16/32/64 up), not 1.25, and never states a 1.25 floor. Utopia.fyi's ratio presets (1.067-1.333 etc.) are documented for TYPE scale, not spacing, and its spacing calculator carries no minimum-ratio recommendation. Neither source actually endorses 1.25 for spacing; the number's only real anchor is the unrelated typographic modular-scale naming convention (Minor Third/Major Third), applied to whitespace purely by analogy. This does not kill the CONV working-threshold (the draft already treats it as advisory-only, never a gate), but the citation as written overclaims what EightShapes/Utopia actually say.

S19: GitHub Projects framed as a platform-convention anchor for a fixed priority scale is overclaimed: GitHub's own docs confirm Priority is NOT a built-in default field, it is a user-created custom single-select field with no canonical option set (their own example uses Low/Medium/High, not the draft's implied Urgent/High/Medium/Low). The draft's 'Urgent vs No Priority, most items ungraded' observation is one team's ad hoc field configuration, not a GitHub Projects convention. Downgraded from a platform-convention anchor to a weak/anecdotal data point.

S19: Miro cited as a '3-tier' convention anchor for the low end of the tier-count band is overclaimed: Miro is a general whiteboard/diagramming tool with no native priority or severity feature (confirmed via miro.com/features, no tagging-tier system described). The captured '3-tier embedded table' reflects one board's freeform design choice, not a Miro-endorsed convention. Downgraded from convention anchor to weak/anecdotal data point; the tier-count band's real anchors are Jira (5, native field) and ClickUp (4, native field), both confirmed canonical.

S19: Airtable group-header format quoted as 'literally PRIORITY [tier] + Count N' overclaims precision for what is more plausibly a paraphrase of the UI, not a verbatim string; softened to a description rather than a quoted literal in verified_addition.

S20: Airbnb's cited "6-level breadcrumb (Home > All topics > Searching and booking > Booking places to stay > Booking basics > Booking split stays)" is not a verified capture. Mobbin spot-check of Airbnb's actual Help Center found 5-level breadcrumbs on different topics (Home/All topics/Legal terms/Privacy Policy/Airbnb Privacy; Home/All topics/Payments, pricing and refunds/Paying for a reservation/When you'll pay for your reservation), and a search for the exact 'Searching and booking > Booking places to stay > Booking basics > Booking split stays' path returned no matching screen. This is the classic pattern the myth_screen exists to catch: a real, correctly-named paper wearing an invented precise statistic. Downgraded and softened in verified_addition -- the qualitative claim (search and browse are mixed, not a fixed user-type split) survives on the real paper's actual finding; the 70/30 number does not.
